transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because my sleep has really fallen apart. I’ll be in bed for hours, laptop closed, but my mind is still going over work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments… it just doesn’t stop. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really turned off.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

Yes. I worry about normal things way more than I think I should. My mind jumps from whether I’m falling behind at work, to whether school is a waste of money, to whether my family thinks I can’t handle things. Even small issues feel like they could mess up my whole future.
Have you experienced any traumatic events in your life?
Not really, no. I mean, nothing I would think of as a traumatic event. I’ve had stressful periods, but not something like that.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain activities or places because of your worries?

Yeah… I don’t know if it’s specific places exactly, but I’ve definitely started avoiding things I used to do because I feel too overwhelmed. I’m missing work deadlines, falling behind in my certificate classes, and I’ve stopped doing the routines that used to help me stay steady, like yoga, running, and cooking. It’s like I know those things would help, but I just can’t get myself to keep up with them.
Are there specific social situations or events that you've been avoiding because you fear something might go wrong or you might feel overwhelmed?

I’m not sure it’s specific social situations. I don’t think I’m avoiding people because I’m afraid something embarrassing will happen or anything like that. It’s more that if something feels like too much to deal with, I’ll put it off or not go, but I can’t point to one type of event specifically.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of sadness or hopelessness lately?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless, exactly. I’ve been stressed and worn down, but I haven’t noticed a deep sadness in the way you mean, I don’t think.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or anxiety that reach a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so. I feel anxious a lot, but I haven’t noticed it coming on suddenly and peaking within a few minutes like that.
Do you feel anxious most of the time, even when there's no obvious reason for it?

Yes. A lot of the time it doesn’t even feel like there’s one clear reason. My mind just jumps around—from worrying I’m falling behind at work, to whether I’m wasting money on school, to whether my family thinks I can’t handle things. Even small problems start feeling like they could mess up my whole future.
Do you find yourself repeating certain thoughts or behaviors over and over, feeling like you can't control them?

Yes, kind of. I don’t have like a ritual, but I get stuck on worries. I’ll try to tell myself to stop and just focus on one thing, but then one worry turns into another. Before I know it I’m checking my calendar, my budget, and my assignments over and over, instead of actually getting anything done.
Do you feel an overwhelming urge to perform specific mental acts or behaviors in response to your worries?

I wouldn’t say it’s a specific ritual I have to do, but I do feel pushed to check things when I’m worried. I’ll try to stop and focus on one thing, and then another worry pops up, and before I know it I’m going back through my calendar, my budget, or my assignments over and over instead of actually doing what I need to do.
Do you feel like these repetitive behaviors, such as checking your calendar or budget, are something you must do to prevent something bad from happening?

I’m not sure I’d say I believe it prevents something bad from happening. It’s more like I feel uneasy if I don’t check, like I won’t be able to settle down. But I don’t have a clear thought like, “If I don’t do this, something terrible will happen.”
Do you believe that checking your calendar, budget, or assignments repeatedly helps to prevent something specific from going wrong?

Not really something specific. It’s more that I can’t get the worry to stop. I’ll tell myself to just focus on one thing, but then another worry comes up right away, and then I’m checking my calendar, my budget, my assignments over and over. It feels like I’m trying to calm myself down, but I just end up not getting anything done.
Do you feel like these repetitive checking behaviors are helping to reduce your anxiety?

Maybe for a moment, but not really. I try to tell myself to stop and just focus on one thing, but then another worry comes up right away. Then I’m checking my calendar, my budget, my assignments again and again, and I end up stuck instead of actually getting anything done.
Do you feel like you're checking your calendar, budget, or assignments because you have an irresistible urge to do so?

It does feel hard to resist, yeah. I’ll tell myself to stop and just focus on one thing, but then another worry pops up right away. Before I know it, I’m checking my calendar, my budget, and my assignments over and over, and I’m not actually getting anything done.
Do you believe these checking behaviors are intended to prevent something bad or unwanted from happening?

Not really like I’m preventing one specific bad thing. It’s more that I can’t shut the worry off. I try to stop and focus on one thing, but then another worry comes up, and I end up checking my calendar, budget, and assignments over and over instead of getting anything done.
Do you think your worries and anxiety started after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yeah, I think it started after a big change. It’s been going on for about a year and three months, since I started an evening graduate certificate program while still working full-time as an analyst. Since then, the worrying has just kind of stayed with me.
Did your excessive worrying and anxiety start shortly after you began your graduate certificate program and working full-time?
Yes. It started pretty soon after I began the evening certificate program while keeping my full-time analyst job. It’s been going on about a year and three months now.
Do you feel like your repetitive checking behaviors are aimed at reducing anxiety triggered by specific, distressing thoughts?

Yes, I think so. It’s like the anxiety builds from one worry to the next, and I try to tell myself to stop and just focus on one thing, but I can’t. Then I end up checking my calendar, my budget, and my assignments again and again, instead of actually getting anything done.
Do you think your worries and anxiety are primarily related to the stress of managing both work and your graduate certificate program?

Yes, mostly. It feels tied to trying to manage both, but it spreads into everything. My mind jumps from worrying I’m falling behind at work, to thinking I’m wasting money on school, to worrying my family will think I can’t handle it. Even small problems start feeling like they could mess up my whole future.
Do you think your worries and anxiety would improve if you were able to find a way to better manage the stress of your work and graduate certificate program?

I think it probably would help, yes. A lot of it feels tied to not being able to keep up with both things. My mind just keeps jumping around—like, am I falling behind at work, am I wasting money on school, is my family going to think I can’t handle things. And then even something small starts feeling like it could ruin everything or derail my future.
